'''''Gilia tricolor''''' ('''bird's-eyes''', '''bird's-eye gilia''', '''tricolor gilia''') is an [[annual plant|annual]] [[flowering plant]] in the phlox family ([[Polemoniaceae]]).<ref name=SNW>Sierra Nevada Wildflowers, Karen Wiese, 2013, p. 49</ref>

==Range and habitat==
It is native to the [[Central Valley (California)|Central Valley]] and foothills of the [[Sierra Nevada (U.S.)|Sierra Nevada]] and [[California Coast Ranges|Coast Ranges]] in California.<ref name=SNW/> Its native habitats include open, grassy plains and slopes below {{Convert|2000|ft|meters}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center - The University of Texas at Austin|url=https://www.wildflower.org/plants/result.php?id_plant=GITR2|access-date=2021-12-26|website=www.wildflower.org}}</ref> However, there has been some sighting reported on iNaturalist in Western Washington and Southern Western Canada.

===Inflorescence and fruit===
Flowers have 5 green sepals and 5 bell-shaped fused petals, which are blue-violet at the end, descending to purple spots over yellow throats, hence the three for "tri".<ref name=SNW/>

==Human uses==
Seeds of this plant are sold online as a [[flower garden|garden flower]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.outsidepride.com/seed/flower-seed/gilia/gilia-tricolor.html |title=GiliaTricolor Bird's Eye Drought Resistant Flower Seed for Xeriscape Gardening }}</ref>
